newsitem.title: GUAM: Seoul experts to help identify Guam crash victims.
newsitem.headline: Seoul experts to help identify Guam crash victims.

text.p: The South Korean government has sent five forensic experts to help identify the bodies of people killed in last week's crash in Guam of a Korean Air Lines jet, officials said on Thursday.

More than 200 people died and 28 survived when a KAL Boeing 747 ploughed into a hillside about five km (three miles) from Guam's international airport. Seventy-one of more than 150 bodies recovered have been identified, officials said.

Clifford Guzman, special assistant to the Guam governor, said recovery and identification of bodies were being undertaken by KAL, the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board, the U.S. and Guam governments and the five Korean specialists.
"This way there will be no confusion...as to the type of information that is getting to you," he told a briefing for reporters and relatives of the crash victims.
"Please understand that we are all working very hard together ... to bring your loved ones to you."
Recovery operations have been hampered by rugged terrain and, earlier this week, by heavy monsoon rains.
